correctness.rationale: The Hodge star maps each simplicial-boundary (n-2)-subset generator to a signed u∧e_i∧e_j. Its Gram matrix is nI-D^T D, equal to n times the orthogonal projection onto the K_n cycle space since DD^T=nI-11^T. Hence the centered zonotope is isometric to sqrt(n)Pi[-1/2,1/2]^m in dimension C(n-1,2). A nonzero facet normal is a minimal-support circulation, necessarily an oriented simple cycle, yielding distance sqrt(n ell)/2 and count C(n,ell)(ell-1)!. Triangle circulations span, enforcing unique origin incenter. At cube corners squared norm is (nm-||D sigma||²)/4; parity and existence of (almost-)regular tournaments give extremal imbalance 0 (odd n) or n (even), and expose the contacts. Invariance under the irreducible S_n cycle-space representation plus uniqueness of John/Loewner ellipsoids makes them the computed centered Euclidean balls. Independent parity enumeration confirms 24 and 2640 contact signed corners at n=5,6 and facet counts 74,394.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration proves n=5,6 tests only; general statement rests on Hodge, graphic-matroid cocircuit support and irreducible representation.

value.rationale: The near-top acyclohedron is a natural infinite parameter family already studied combinatorially. The theorem gives its canonical Euclidean realization, exact facets by cycle length, sharp two radii, uniqueness and symmetry of extremal ellipsoids, and a parity-sensitive combinatorial characterization of outer contacts. These are coherent structural invariants, with applications to geometric comparisons of cographic zonotopes, not arbitrary numerical slices.
residual_risks: Not an arbitrary-uniformity classification; no closed formula for counts of all regular tournaments required.
